jobs.title: Associate Environmental Specialist
jobs.description:
Job Overview:

At the Metropolitan Water District of Southern California, we deliver reliable water to a region with 19 million people—and to accomplish this, we rely on a team of talented employees: innovators, problem-solvers, and collaborators who make it all possible.

There is currently one (1) opening for Associate Environmental Specialist located at Headquarters, Los Angeles, CA.

This recruitment may result in an eligibility list\*.

**JOB SUMMARY**

As an Associate Environmental Specialist, you will coordinate compliance programs across multiple Metropolitan facilities. In this role, you will develop and implement programs related to hazardous materials, air quality, wastewater, and underground storage tanks. You will be responsible for updating the environmental management database and ensuring tasks are completed timely. You will play a key role in maintaining regulatory compliance, creating training materials tailored to stakeholders and fostering collaborative relationships with internal teams and external regulatory agencies.

**What You’ll Do**

* **Environmental Project & Compliance Management:** Develop and conduct environmental assessments, plans, and permitting projects across multiple regional sites, focusing on hazardous materials, air quality, and wastewater management.
* **Regulatory Reporting & Database Management:** Utilize key state and local databases—including CERS, GeoTracker, SCAQMD Permit Database, CalOES Spill Reporting Database, and DTSC Hazardous Waste Tracking System—to ensure complete and accurate compliance reporting.
* **Digital Records & System Optimization:** Modernize Environmental, Health and Safety (EHS) records using SharePoint and cloud-based collaboration platforms; evaluate and recommend updated tools and systems as operational needs evolve.
* **Regulatory Monitoring & Advice:** Track federal, state, and local environmental laws, regulations, and emerging issues to evaluate their impact on Metropolitan operations and advise on compliance strategy.
* **Stakeholder Engagement & Agency Relations:** Serve as a clear, proactive communicator to build and maintain positive relationships with internal partners and external regulatory agencies.

This job announcement has been designed to indicate the general nature and level of work being performed by employees in this classification / job.

To view the full job description click here: **Associate Environmental Specialist**

**Schedule: 9/80** Start times are no earlier than 6 am and end times are no later than 6 pm.

**Hybrid:** Metropolitan’s current practice in this position is a hybrid work schedule. This typically includes two days a week in person and the other days remote. This is subject to change dependent on organizational needs. In addition, a telework policy is scheduled for negotiations and once completed and implemented, will provide final direction on the hybrid schedule.

**EMPLOYMENT STANDARDS MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**

**Education and Experience:** Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university in a related field and four years of relevant experience; or two years in an MWD Assistant Environmental Specialist II classification; or Masters degree from an accredited college or university in a related field and two years of relevant experience.

**Relevant/Related Experience is defined as:** work experience with environmental, health and safety compliance programs to comply with local, county, state and federal requirements, including Air Quality, Underground Storage Tanks, Industrial Wastewater, Stormwater and Hazardous Materials/Waste.

**Related Degree is defined as:** an area within Engineering, Environmental Science, Biology, Ecology, Planning or other related fields.

**CERTIFICATIONS, LICENSES, AND REGISTRATION REQUIREMENTS**

Employees in this position may be required to obtain and maintain the following certifications, licensing and registrations:

**License(s):** Valid California Class C Driver’s License or equivalent **(required at time of application)** that allows you to drive during your employment.

**BENEFITS**

* Competitive compensation
* Excellent medical, dental, life, vision plans.
* Deferred compensation in the form of a 401(k) plan (with matching contribution) and a 457 plan.
* Retirement benefits under the California Public Employees' Retirement System
* Tuition reimbursement
* Training and advancement opportunities
* Excellent working environment
* Public transportation reimbursements
* Hub of public transportation: rail, subway, buses, and taxis
* On-site fitness center

For more information on MWD benefits, please use the following link: **Benefits Regular FT PT Employees (Represented)**

**ABOUT MWD**

The Metropolitan Water District of Southern California is a state-established cooperative that, along with its 26 cities and retail suppliers, provides water for 19 million people in six counties. The district imports water from the Colorado River and Northern California to supplement local supplies, and helps its members to develop increased water conservation, recycling, storage and other resource-management programs.

Metropolitan is an Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) employer. The Metropolitan Water District of Southern California is committed to fostering an inclusive and respectful workplace for all employees.

Qualified individuals with disabilities who need a reasonable accommodation during the application or selection process, please reach out to the Human Resources Office at (213) 217-7738 or email jobs@mwdh2o.com.

In accordance with applicable laws, we provide religious accommodations for sincerely held religious beliefs, practices, and observances that conflict with work requirements. If you require a religious accommodation during the application, interview, or employment process, please reach out to the EEO Office at (213) 217-5858 or eeooffice@mwdh2o.com. Requests are evaluated on a case-by-case basis.

jobs.title: Senior Environmental Scientist
jobs.description:
**Senior Environmental Scientist**

**Perth, WA | Permanent, Full-time / Part-time**

RPS, a Tetra Tech company, is a leading global professional services consultancy delivering solutions across the environment, infrastructure, energy and urban development sectors.

In Australia Asia Pacific, we work with industry, government and communities to define, design and manage complex projects that create shared value. Our people combine technical expertise with practical thinking to help clients understand environmental risks, navigate complex challenges and deliver successful project outcomes.

As part of Tetra Tech, we are connected to a global network of approximately 30,000 employees, providing access to specialist expertise, opportunities and projects across Australia and internationally.

**The Opportunity**

We are seeking a Senior Scientist to join our Oceans & Environment team in Perth, or Margaret River. RPS understand the importance of flexible working arrangements and this role is open to both full-time and part-time hours.

This is an excellent opportunity for an early to mid career environmental scientist who has experience in environmental approvals and is looking to continue developing their technical and consulting capability. Working alongside experienced environmental professionals, you will contribute to a range of projects.

**What you'll be involved in**

Your responsibilities will include:

* Preparing environmental approval documentation under the EP Act and EPBC Act.
* Preparing practical environmental management plans and strategies.
* Prepare and provide environmental advice to clients.
* Manage multiple tasks on a range of projects and effectively deal with conflicting priorities and work to tight deadlines.
* Prepare and provide environmental advice to clients.
* Work as part of a multi-disciplinary team and work co-operatively with people at all levels to achieve outcomes.
* Communicate and maintain good relationships with internal stakeholders, clients, suppliers and project stakeholders.

**About you**

We are looking for someone who is technically curious, practical and keen to build a career in environmental approvals and environmental consulting.

**You will ideally bring:**

* A relevant tertiary qualification in environmental management or environmental science.
* Experience in undertaking environmental impact assessments in Western Australia.
* Understanding of State and Commonwealth environmental legislation, policy and guidance.
* Good technical report writing skills and attention to detail
* Minimum of five years relevant work experience.
* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
* Strong communication and interpersonal skills
* The ability to work independently while knowing when to seek technical guidance
* An understanding of project delivery including quality, safety, time and budget considerations
* A commitment to ongoing professional and technical development

**Why RPS?**

Joining RPS means becoming part of a collaborative environmental team while also having access to the technical capability and opportunities of the broader Tetra Tech network.

You will have the opportunity to develop your career alongside experienced contaminated land specialists, gain exposure to a diverse range of projects and progressively take on greater technical, project and client responsibilities.

**We also offer:**

* Flexible and hybrid working arrangements where appropriate
* Professional development and career progression opportunities
* Paid professional memberships
* Active lifestyle and wellbeing initiatives
* Employee assistance and wellbeing support
* Opportunities to work with technical specialists across Australia and the wider Tetra Tech network
* A supportive and collaborative team environment
* Paid parental leave and other employee benefits

**Our commitment**

RPS is committed to creating an inclusive workplace where people are respected, supported and encouraged to bring their individual perspectives and experience to work.

If you have a foundation in environmental science or contaminated land and are looking for an opportunity to deepen your technical expertise while working alongside experienced specialists, we'd like to hear from you.

**Our Approach**

Our people live our purpose, deliver our promise, and demonstrate our behaviours every day. Our behaviours define who we are. Developed by our people, they underpin everything that we do. They create the memorable experiences we are known for and make RPS a great place to do great work.  
Stronger together is one of our five core behaviours and it is key to building a collaborative workplace. We encourage everyone to bring their best and to support others to do the same. By sharing knowledge, challenging each other to think differently, and fostering an environment of trust and respect, our people can learn, grow and thrive – and share in our success.

**Recruitment Agencies**

We have a Preferred Supplier List of trusted partners to assist us when required and do not acknowledge any speculative CVs or unsolicited candidate introductions from agencies not on this list. Please refer to the careers page on our website if you require any further information.

jobs.title: Hydrogeologist / Water Resources Specialist
jobs.description:
**Job Summary**

The Energy and Security Group seeks a Hydrologist / Water Resources Engineer for an upcoming assignment for commercial shale and tight oil and gas development in South Asia.

**Responsibilities**

* Map surface water and groundwater availability, quality and competing uses for pilot and candidate development areas.
* Quantify pilot and development water demand under alternative completion designs.
* Assess floodwater capture and storage, brackish groundwater, treated effluent and produced-water reuse.
* Develop water sourcing strategy: source mix, conveyance and storage, seasonal logic and recycling targets, with costs for the financial model.
* Design groundwater baseline monitoring and assess abstraction and contamination pathways for the ESIA.

**Qualifications**

* Master's degree in hydrogeology, water resources engineering, or related field.
* 12+ years in water resource assessment, including water sourcing for oil and gas or unconventional operations.

Pay: $500.00 - $1,200.00 per day

Work Location: Remote
